hints: Choose a new letter that differs from the original cell's letter.
For each cell, also avoid letters already assigned to its up and left neighbors; these are the earlier adjacent cells in row-major order.
There are four letters and at most three forbidden choices, so one always remains.
analogy: Color cells in reading order, avoiding the old color and the two neighbors already painted.
example: If a cell originally has A and its up and left neighbors are B and C, choose D; it differs from all three constraints.
algorithm: Scan row-major and try A through D until finding one unequal to the original character and the final characters above and left; output it.
correctness: Every edge joins a cell to an earlier or later neighbor; the later endpoint checks the earlier endpoint, so all adjacent cells differ and each changed cell differs from its input.
complexity: O(nm) time and O(nm) space if storing the result.
